Spin-independent WIMP sensitivity of an LZ-like xenon TPC — a forward model validated against LZ WS2024

Supporting Documents
  • ✨ASTRA Inventory

Summary¶

This project builds, from public information only, a forward model of a dual-phase xenon dark-matter experiment modeled on LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ), and uses it to compute the median sensitivity to spin-independent WIMP–nucleon scattering. No observed events are used. NEST microphysics maps a WIMP signal and each of LZ’s twelve WS2024 background sources into corrected observables (S1c, log10 S2c). A binned two-dimensional profile likelihood then turns these templates into a median expected limit for the WS2024 exposure of 3.3 tonne-years.

The validation target is LZ’s WS2024-only median expected limit, 5.76 × 10⁻⁴⁸ cm² at 40 GeV/c², from slide 24 of the collaboration’s TeVPA talk. It is like-for-like with our exposure. LZ’s combined 4.2 tonne-year result (5.1 × 10⁻⁴⁸ cm²) also includes the WS2022 sample, which we do not model.

At 40 GeV/c², our median power-constrained limit is 5.39e-48 cm² (bootstrap uncertainty 1.1e-49 cm²). That is within the agreed 25% of LZ’s value, and the curve tracks LZ’s across the published mass range (◆Validation 5: median sensitivity vs LZ WS2024-only). An independent Feldman–Cousins cut-and-count analysis gives 5.7e-48 cm² at the same mass. All seven validations along the chain pass (see the table below).

FINDING
The binned 2D profile-likelihood median sensitivity (power-constrained, toy Neyman construction, 3.3 tonne-years) is 5.39e-48 +/- 0.11e-48 cm2 at 40 GeV/c2 vs LZ's WS2024-only median 5.76e-48 (ratio 0.935), passing the 25% acceptance (A1). At all 22 masses where LZ's +/-1 sigma band is published our median lies inside it (A2); ratios to LZ span 0.85-1.18: about 1.18 at 13-17 GeV/c2, 1.02-1.08 at 19-32, 0.94-0.96 at 36-46 and 0.85-0.94 from 65 GeV/c2 up.
WS2024 exposure only (uniform_1d, combined_single as one pooled WS2024 sample, two-sided q, power constraint at -1 sigma); 25 mu points 0.5-40 events, 2000 toys per mu, 1000 background-only toys, seed 20261118.
The original A1 gate (|ours - LZ| <= 2 bootstrap sigma) failed with pull -3.5 because it ignored the uncertainty of LZ's curve and its digitization and our binned single-sample approximation of LZ's unbinned six-sample likelihood; the user set the 25% criterion on 2026-11-19. The low-mass excess and high-mass deficit are not investigated. Band comparisons use our unconstrained toy quantiles (LZ's convention). Nothing was tuned.

Projection to 1000 live days¶

The same machinery, with signal and every background scaled to 1000 live days (fractional background uncertainties held fixed), gives a 40 GeV/c² median of 1.97e-48 cm² from the profile likelihood, versus 2.34e-48 cm² from cut-and-count. At the WS2024 exposure, the two methods agree within about 10%. Both counting regions optimize to nearly background-free (about 0.7 expected events), where the extra shape information adds little. With more exposure, the likelihood’s use of the whole (S1c, log10 S2c) plane starts to pay off above about 20 GeV/c².

The analysis was built in stages: microphysics, then backgrounds, then signal, then statistics. Each stage was validated before the next was run.

Model¶

Configuration and decisions¶

The analysis is declared in astra.yaml; every choice below is a named decision, with alternatives and rationale. The consequential ones:

  • Response: NEST itself, through the nestpy bindings, with LZ’s published WS2024 detector header (◇Detector response / microphysics model, ◇NEST version / detector parameter pinning). Active: NEST library via nestpy bindings, WS2024 parameter set (NEST 2.4.0).

  • Detector effects: Uniform 1D response (no position effects). A uniform response means LZ-style position corrections are the identity, so everything lives directly in corrected space (S1c, log10 S2c) (◇Position-dependent detector effects in the response).

  • Backgrounds: every WS2024 Table I source simulated individually (◇Background components simulated); accidentals built from LZ’s factorized construction, constrained by the WS2024 Fig. 3 contours (◇Accidental-coincidence 2D model from public sources).

  • Efficiencies: public curves as inputs, applied in stages with the ROI applied exactly once (◇Signal analysis efficiency, ◇Electron-recoil staged selection treatment; see Efficiency methodology).

  • Statistics: binned 2D profile likelihood as the primary method, with Feldman–Cousins cut-and-count as a cross-check (◇Statistical inference machinery). Median of background-only toy limits (◇Definition of the median sensitivity), two-sided test statistic (◇Two-sided vs one-sided test statistic), power constraint at −1σ (◇Power constraint on the limit), and standard halo parameters, fixed rather than profiled (◇Astrophysical (halo) model).

  • Exposure: a single combined sample (◇Exposure / likelihood sample structure), realized as the WS2024 3.3 tonne-years.

The full decision registry, with every option, is in the appendix.

Stage 1 — microphysics¶

◆Calibrated microphysics response drives NEST’s own FullCalculation/GetS1/GetS2 chain with the WS2024 detector header. On its own, NEST reproduces LZ’s published g2, extraction efficiency and single-electron size from the header parameters. The ER calibration band uses the true tritium β spectrum (◇ER calibration source spectrum (band generation)).

Stage 5 — statistics¶

The primary result, ◆2D PLR median sensitivity curve, is a binned Poisson likelihood over the (S1c, log10 S2c) plane, with all twelve background rates as Gaussian-constrained nuisance parameters. Limits come from a toy-MC Neyman construction, using 2000 signal toys per tested signal strength and 1000 background-only toys per mass. The likelihood core reproduces the exact one-bin Feldman–Cousins intervals.

The cross-check, ◆Cut-and-count FC sensitivity curve, optimizes a counting region per mass by signal-to-background ranking. It evaluates the median FC limit exactly from the Poisson median count, so no toys are needed.

The FC optimum sits at n_med = 0 (B about 0.68) above 20 GeV/c2, a near-background-free regime where the 2D shape adds little; this explains the closeness. FC retained signal fraction 0.44-0.92. The counting regions sit in regions of sparse background MC (documented limitation) and the FC calculation has no background uncertainty.

Limitations¶

  • Exposure: WS2024’s 3.3 tonne-years only. LZ’s combined result adds WS2022, which needs its own response, efficiency and backgrounds.

  • Likelihood: binned and single-sample, where LZ’s is unbinned over six samples. The power-constrained −2σ band edge repeats −1σ by construction; the unconstrained bands are stored for comparison with LZ’s.

  • Detector: uniform response. Position-dependent broadening is the likely cause of the residual NR band width in the WS2024 configuration, and of the deep low-charge tail in Validation 4. simplified_position is the escalation option.

  • Efficiencies: applied as energy-conditional averages. The full unpublished dependence on S1c, S2c and position is not recoverable.

  • Fixed inputs: background constraints use Table I pre-fit uncertainties. Halo parameters are fixed.

Efficiency methodology¶

These sections document how the public efficiency curves are applied, and the before/after comparisons that justified each choice. The comparisons are cross-checks, not acceptance gates. The model that results passes Validations 1–7.

Staged NR efficiency¶

The public Fig. 2 efficiency is a sequence of selections, not a single pre-response factor. The cumulative total already includes the S2 and S1 ROI. The choice of energy-space selection is explicit in ◇Signal analysis efficiency; the active treatment is Pre-ROI input curve then explicit observable ROI.

For the corrected chain, only the pre-ROI trigger plus SS/data-analysis stage is applied in recoil-energy space. NEST and the explicit corrected-observable ROI follow once, before Table I normalization. Consequently this correction changes NR generation efficiencies and shapes, but not the imposed central physical Table I counts. It is also the chain used for the absolute WIMP signal yields.

◆Matched NR efficiency correction comparison reruns complete, matched-budget background models under the legacy and corrected selections. It retains full Monte Carlo histograms, unit-area NR shape comparisons, and both evaluations of the exclusive-total Validation 4 gates. The independent-seed, fivefold-budget B8+hep study distinguishes sparse-bin fluctuations from the effect of the efficiency change.

Staged ER efficiency¶

Electron-recoil selection follows the public cumulative stages of ▤Public ER efficiencies, LZ arXiv:2511.17350v1 rather than treating the published total efficiency as another independent weight. The active choice is Trigger before NEST, native coincidence plus S1, then conditional G/Y.

For each sampled true recoil energy, the public trigger curve B(E) is applied before NEST. NEST’s own threefold coincidence and the explicit S1c > 3 phd selection follow. Events that pass S1 then receive one conditional single-scatter/data-analysis acceptance C(E) = G(E)/Y(E), evaluated at the retained sampled true energy. Y(E) is the cumulative trigger, coincidence, and lower-S1 efficiency. G(E) is supplied by the public 1D-ROI HEPData curve t3 through 15 keV, where the user identified its overlap with the green SS/data-analysis curve; above 15 keV, G(E) is held at G(15) = 0.959. This is an input convention based on that visual identification, not a separately fitted green curve.

B, Y, and G are not multiplied as three independent efficiencies. The only energy-space selections are B and the one conditional G/Y rejection. The remaining corrected-observable ROI is S1c < 80 phd, S2c ≥ 493 phd, and log10(S2c) < 4.5, applied exactly once. There is no additional raw-S2 cut, threefold coincidence, 1D-analysis energy cut, or total-efficiency factor. NEST does not reconstruct or unfold the true energy used by this selection.

This construction is an energy-dependent average acceptance. It does not recover the unpublished dependence of reconstruction and quality cuts on S1c, S2c, position, or their correlations; that limitation also applies to the NR energy-space treatment. Table I still fixes each background’s central physical mean after selection. Accidentals remain an observable-space model and never pass through this ER energy chain.

◆Complete staged ER efficiency comparison archives complete old/new regeneration of all twelve sources at matched budgets, all eight ER energy- space source shapes, exact NR/accidentals controls, and both evaluations of the six unchanged Validation 4 gates. Cumulative-Y and the independent HEPData total-2D curve are forward diagnostics only: neither is multiplied into the production selection. Both modes pass the same six gates.

Efficiency findings¶

FINDING
The correction replaces the ROI-inclusive total efficiency with the public Fig. 2 pre-ROI stage before NEST and applies the corrected-observable ROI exactly once. In the complete matched-budget A/B, atmospheric-neutrino pre-efficiency acceptance changes from 0.632017 to 0.696642, detector-neutron acceptance from 0.474750 to 0.567192, and B8+hep acceptance from 0.000475 to 0.006578; the corresponding conditional ROI acceptances are 0.935392 -> 0.884960, 0.926821 -> 0.818918, and 0.178947 -> 0.016468. Fixed Table I central physical means are unchanged.
WS2024 response, corrected space, seed 44, n_er=40000, n_nr=120000, n_b8=600000, with independent per-source streams. The independent black/HEPData efficiency input check has maximum residual 0.00136346. These are simulation acceptances, not changes to the Table I physical event rates. This new realization supersedes numerical NR values recorded before the ER source-seeding work.
The controlled comparison reproduces the active declared model exactly, and non-NR arrays and metadata agree except for the intentional efficiency_treatment label. Full unthinned histograms and thinned display samples are separately normalized to Table I. The black total-mode behavior is diagnostic only and is not allowed for absolute WIMP yields.

1. Full-budget production applies the public trigger before NEST, NEST’s own threefold coincidence plus S1c > 3 phd, one conditional SS/data-analysis acceptance G/Y at the retained sampled true energy, and the remaining explicit corrected-space ROI once. G comes from HEPData t3 through 15 keV at the user’s identified green/black overlap and is held at 0.959 above 15 keV. Neither cumulative Y nor independent total-2D t4 is applied as another production factor. No S1 efficiency, coincidence factor, raw-S2 threshold, Erec < 20 keV cut, or total efficiency is applied a second time.¶

The active model reproduces exactly, NR/accidental datasets and metadata match between ER modes, and full/display samples preserve Table-I physical means. The observed NEST coinLevel is 3. Low-Y generated samples receive no arbitrary ratio-one substitution: every energy-space ER source has zero Y<0.01 events after S1. The staged full-ROI plateau-event counts (E>15 keV), ordered 214Pb, Kr85/Ar39/detector gamma, solar ER, 212Pb/218Po, tritium/14C, 136Xe, 124Xe, 127Xe/125Xe are 46, 45, 60, 32, 146, 6, 0, 0. This model does not recover unpublished conditional S1c/S2c/position dependence.

Scope: Public arXiv:2511.17350v1 Fig. 1 and HEPData record 181350 v1 t3/t4 central values; WS2024 NEST response, seed 44, n_er=40000 per ER source, n_nr=120000, n_b8=600000. Per-source seeding isolates unaffected NR and observable-space accidental samples exactly without claiming common random numbers after ER rejection. Fixed Table-I means are not inferred from these MC acceptances.

Output: Complete staged ER efficiency comparison

Output: Per-component background models

Decision registry¶

DECISION
Statistical inference machinery

How the limit/sensitivity is computed from the expected spectra. The plan: 2D binned profile likelihood (primary) plus a cut-and-count with Feldman-Cousins as a transparent cross-check. Note LZ itself used an unbinned PLR — the binned 2D likelihood is a documented approximation to it.

default: 2D binned profile likelihood + FC cut-and-count cross-check · 3 options
DECISION
Background components simulated

Which background sources enter the expectation model as independently simulated, rate-tunable components. WS2022 used nine components; WS2024's Table 1 is the fuller list to extract.

default: Every component in LZ's background table · 3 options
DECISION
Signal analysis efficiency

Event-level cut details are not public, so LZ's published Fig. 2 efficiency is an input. The chain must nevertheless respect the Fig. 2 staging: the pre-ROI curve is applied in recoil-energy space, NEST maps retained recoils to corrected observables, and the observable ROI is applied once. The HEPData t4 black curve already includes both ROI stages, so using it before the same explicit ROI is retained only as a legacy comparison.

default: Pre-ROI input curve then explicit observable ROI · 3 options
DECISION
Electron-recoil staged selection treatment

The public ER Fig. 1 gives cumulative trigger, threefold-coincidence/lower-S1, SS/data-analysis, and total-ROI efficiencies. NEST already simulates the threefold coincidence, so it must not be added again. An energy-space trigger rejection followed by NEST, an explicit lower-S1 selection, one conditional SS/data-analysis acceptance G/Y at the retained true energy, and one remaining observable ROI preserves the public staging without multiplying cumulative curves or treating NEST as an energy unfolding. The user independently verified the green/black overlap through 15 keV and the green high-energy plateau; therefore HEPData t3 supplies G through 15 keV and G(15) is held above it. This is an average energy-conditional cut model, not the unpublished full dependence of analysis cuts on S1c/S2c/position.

default: Trigger before NEST, native coincidence plus S1, then conditional G/Y · 2 options
DECISION
Detector response / microphysics model

How recoil energy becomes (S1, S2). User decision: use the NEST library itself via the nestpy Python bindings rather than reimplementing the microphysics — LZ's published WS2024 header should work with NEST directly, and the released nestpy wheel ships the LZ_WS2024 detector as a built-in. The HEPData header input (lz_nest_header_hepdata) cross-checks that the packaged detector parameters match LZ's published ones; if they ever disagree, the documented fallback is a source build of nestpy with the header copied into lib/nest. Which parameter set to pin is its own decision (nest_parameter_set).

default: NEST library via nestpy bindings · 3 options
DECISION
Astrophysical (halo) model

Velocity distribution and parameters for the WIMP recoil spectrum. The native pinned TestSpectra implementation provides an SHM at rho0=0.3 GeV/cm3, v0=238 km/s, vesc=544 km/s and V_SUN=250.2 km/s, with its own scalar Earth-speed expression; these are fixed conventions, not profiled parameters or a claim that NEST implements every vector-valued convention-paper detail. LZ's standard-halo choice and the conventions paper fix-parameters guidance motivate this non-default-modulation baseline; the exact code conventions are recorded in the WIMP adapter/provenance and artifacts.

default: Standard halo model, canonical parameters · 2 options
DECISION
Time convention for the non-modulating WIMP projection

NEST's native WIMP day parameter changes the scalar Earth speed and recoil rate; day=0 is a dated realization, not an annual average. This forward model does not perform a modulation analysis. The representative-day default removes the periodic term within NEST's 365.24-day convention and is checked against a direct annual mixture, through the complete response, at the 40 GeV/c2 checkpoint only.

default: Representative day with zero periodic Earth-speed term · 2 options
DECISION
High-recoil support of NEST's native WIMP preparation

The native WIMP preparation integrates 0-100 keVnr, but high WIMP masses have a non-negligible folded recoil tail beyond it. Dropping or rescaling that tail would change absolute yields. The extension samples NEST's own exposed WIMP_dRate density beyond the preparation support, adds the native tail integral, and records the unadded far-tail guard. This is numerical support accounting, not another recoil model.

default: Sample native dRate above the prepared 0-100 keVnr integral · 2 options
DECISION
NEST version / detector parameter pinning

LZ's two campaigns used different NEST versions and detector parameter sets: WS2022 tuned NEST 2.3.7 (g1 = 0.114 phd/photon, g2 = 47.1 phd/electron, SES 58.5 phd, extraction 80.5%); WS2024 tuned NEST 2.4.0 (g1 = 0.112 +/- 0.002, g2 = 34.0 +/- 0.9, SES 46.9 phd, extraction 72.5%), with a reproducing header file on HEPData. The validation target is the WS2024 median sensitivity, so the WS2024 set is the natural default.

default: WS2024 parameter set (NEST 2.4.0) · 3 options
DECISION
Two-sided vs one-sided test statistic

LZ uses a two-sided profile likelihood ratio test statistic, and the community conventions recommend the two-sided PLR (their Eq. 4), noting it equals the Feldman-Cousins construction when nuisance parameters are absent. A one-sided (CLs-style) variant is a common alternative worth having on the decision space.

default: Two-sided PLR (LZ / conventions) · 2 options
DECISION
Power constraint on the limit

LZ power-constrains the limit at all masses to 1 sigma below the median expectation (WS2022 used pi_crit = 0.16 between 13 and 36 GeV/c2), which prevents downward fluctuations from producing overly strong limits at the cost of overcoverage. Whether to apply it changes the reported curve and is a standard methodological fork.

default: Power constraint applied (LZ) · 2 options
DECISION
Definition of the median sensitivity

The validation target is LZ's median expected limit. LZ obtains it as the median of expected limits from background-only pseudo-experiments with post-fit background estimates (green/yellow bands in Fig. 5), consistent with the conventions paper's recommendation of toy Monte Carlo over asymptotic formulae. A single Asimov-dataset limit is the cheaper alternative and coincides with the median up to construction details.

default: Median of toy-MC expected limits (LZ) · 3 options
DECISION
Exposure / likelihood sample structure

LZ splits the data into six likelihood samples (four WS2024 flow-state/radon-tag categories plus a veto-tagged sample plus the full WS2022 sample) with some nuisance parameters independent between flow states. For a forward model with no observed data, pooling into a single sample reproduces the expected total counts exactly and only neglects the nuisance-decoupling benefit of the split. As realized, the pooled sample is the WS2024 exposure alone (3.3 tonne-years, Table I scope); adding WS2022's 0.9 tonne-years to reach LZ's combined 4.2 needs a separately validated WS2022 response, efficiency, ROI and background set and is not implemented.

default: Single combined exposure (simplified) · 2 options
DECISION
Position-dependent detector effects in the response

LZ's NEST-based application additionally models curved electron drift paths from field non-uniformities, finite position reconstruction resolution, and position-dependence of S1/S2 sizes. These widen the S1/S2 bands beyond pure microphysics fluctuations; LZ's NEST tuning compensates with reduced band widths (and skewness disabled in WS2022). A uniform 1D response with LZ's tuned band widths is the simplest model that can still reproduce the published band shapes.

default: Uniform 1D response (no position effects) · 2 options
DECISION
ER calibration source spectrum (band generation)

The ER calibration bands are conditional on the tritium source spectrum: at fixed S1c, events from higher energy sit at higher S2c, so over-weighting the high-energy tail biases the simulated band median upward at high S1c. A flat spectrum between threshold and the 18.6 keVee endpoint was the initial approximation and showed exactly that signature (medians up to +0.6% too high at S1c 70-79 in both configurations, and a localized width residual at S1c > 65 in WS2022); the true tritium beta spectrum removes it (WS2022 max width residual 6.0% -> 3.6%; WS2024 max median deviation 0.64% -> 0.36%). The NR analogue needs no such choice: a monoenergetic 2.45 MeV DD neutron gives an exactly flat single-scatter recoil spectrum.

default: True tritium beta spectrum · 2 options
DECISION
Accidental-coincidence 2D model from public sources

Accidentals are a data-driven LZ background (no simulation), and the WS2024-only limit's underfluctuation is attributed to them, so their 2D shape matters. Only public material is used (LZ-internal model documents are off-limits by project decision). Two public constraints exist: the WS2024 Fig. 3 68%/95% quantile contours (vector-digitized, lz_ws2024_accidentals_contours) and the SR1 Fig. 12 marginal functions of the companion paper (raster-digitized, lz_accidentals_marginals_sr1). Because LZ's construction is exactly factorized (outer product of the S1 and S2 marginals, insight lz_accidentals_factorized_pdf), a P(S1c)*P(log10 S2c) model reconstructed from the WS2024 contours is well-posed: two nested contours constrain the two marginals, and the SR1 marginals are then an independent morphology cross-check (LZ states the WS2024 method is identical to the SR1 one).

default: Factorized PDF constrained by WS2024 Fig. 3 contours · 2 options

Outputs¶

Outputs
OutputTypeDescription
response_model_calibration Calibrated microphysics responsedataCalibrated NEST-style response engine outputs, consumed by every later stage: ER and NR light/charge yields vs recoil energy at the LZ drift field, and the ER/NR band medians and widths in (S1c, log10 S2c) space, written as lookup tables. Uses the NEST header input for detector parameters.python src/build_response_model.py --output {output}
er_band_validation Validation 1: ER band vs LZfigureValidation of the microphysics stage: the response engine (the same GetYields -> GetQuanta -> GetS1/GetS2 nestpy chain as build_response_model.py) run in the WS2022 configuration that the digitized reference corresponds to (nestpy LZ_WS2022 detector, drift field 192 V/cm from FitEF, tritium events sampled from the true tritium beta spectrum p·E·(E0−E)²·F(Z=2,E) up to the 18.590 keV endpoint per decision calibration_er_spectrum — the initial flat-spectrum approximation over-weighted the endpoint and biased the high-S1c medians up by up to +0.6% with a localized width residual at S1c > 65, both removed by the true spectrum; toggle kept via --er-spectrum flat), 1M events, ROI S2c > 600 phd re-applied at analysis level, overlaid on the digitized LZ tritium ER band. Version bridges from NEST v2.3.7 (what LZ SR1 ran) to the NEST master that nestpy vendors: NRERWidthsParam[6] passed negated (v2.4.x treats [6] > 0 as absolute Fano, [6] < 0 reproduces v2.3.7's additive term); [8]/[9] swapped (v2.3.7 reads [8] = omega width, [9] = center; master reads [8] = center, [9] = width); SkewnessER = 0.0 for ER (the header's instruction); er_parameters = the [-1]x10 sentinel (master's GetYieldBetaGR is parameterized and a positive vector would override the hardcoded v2.3.7 ER model); width vector padded with two zeros to 13 elements. The chain was verified semantically equivalent to v2.3.7 by source-level diffing (RandomGen, GetYields, GetQuanta, GetS1/GetS2 total-area paths). ACCEPTANCE: band median agrees to better than 5% relative in log10(S2c) over every comparable reference bin (achieved: max 0.54%, inside LZ's own 1% NR-mean tuning bar, insight lz_nest_er_band_tuning); band width (the (q90-q10)/2 half-width) within 5% relative OR 0.0065 absolute in log10(S2c), the floor being the digitized reference's own curve resolution. Result: max width deviation 3.6% (0.0037 abs) — previously 6.0% (0.0062 abs) at S1c > 65 under the flat-spectrum approximation, attributed to the spectrum, not the response chain.python src/validate_bands.py --band er --er-spectrum {decisions.calibration_er_spectrum} --reference {inputs.lz_ws2022_band_reference} --header {inputs.lz_ws2022_nest_header} --output {output}
nr_band_validation Validation 2: NR band vs LZfigureValidation of the microphysics stage, NR analogue of er_band_validation: the response engine run in the WS2022 configuration (nestpy LZ_WS2022 detector, the header's edited NRERWidthsParam vector, v2.3.7 default NR yield parameters, drift field 192 V/cm), overlaid on the digitized LZ DD-neutron NR band; DD events drawn ~flat over 1.0-73.5 keVnr (the max Xe recoil from a 2.45 MeV DD neutron, 4mM/(m+M)^2 * E_n — the best physically-motivated approximation of the calibration spectrum; the conditional band width is spectrum-dependent, probed against emax 20-100). Same version bridges and chain-equivalence verification as er_band_validation. ACCEPTANCE: band median within 5% relative (achieved: max 0.44%, inside LZ's own 1% tuning bar); band width within 5% relative OR 0.0065 absolute in log10(S2c) (the reference's own curve resolution). Result: max width deviation 6.9% relative (0.0046 abs) over S1c 40-65, where the reference half-width is narrowest (~0.06-0.08) and relative comparison least well-conditioned; the maximum absolute deviation anywhere is 0.0081 (a wide half-width bin, ~4% relative) — both documented residuals attributed to the reference's provenance (LZ's DD source spectrum and MC statistics are not published), not tuned away.python src/validate_bands.py --band nr --reference {inputs.lz_ws2022_band_reference} --header {inputs.lz_ws2022_nest_header} --output {output}
er_band_validation_ws2024 Validation 1 (WS2024 config): ER band vs LZfigureValidation of the microphysics stage in the configuration the production analysis runs in: the same response engine run in the WS2024 configuration end to end from the HEPData header (nestpy LZ_WS2024 detector, drift field 96.5 V/cm from FitEF, g2 = 34.022 from CalculateG2 vs 34.0 published, tritium events sampled from the true tritium beta spectrum per decision calibration_er_spectrum — the flat approximation biased the high-S1c medians up by up to +0.6%, removed by the true spectrum; toggle kept via --er-spectrum flat, 1M events), overlaid on the digitized slide-9 tritium ER band (lz_ws2024_band_reference). WS2024 version bridges (differ from WS2022): the header ships tuned NRYieldsParam AND ERYieldsParam vectors, passed as-is (positive er_parameters override the hardcoded ER model element-by-element — intended v2.4.0 behavior for this header); NRERWidthsParam[6] = 0.3 passed as-is (an absolute Fano factor under v2.4.0 semantics, no negation); [8]/[9] swapped (the header lists the transposed order; master wants [8] = omega center, [9] = width); ER skewness vector-driven via the SkewnessER = -999 sentinel ([10] = -0.26564 — the header has no disable-instruction); width vector padded to 13; ROI re-applied at analysis level as S2c >= 493 phd = 14.5 extracted electrons x g2 (the slide's calibration scatter is not ROI-cut but its band quantiles evidently were — see src/validate_bands.py). ACCEPTANCE: band median within 5% relative (achieved: max 0.36%); band width within 5% relative OR 0.015 absolute in log10(S2c), the floor being the raster-digitized reference's own curve resolution (measured second-difference noise 0.0020 median / 0.005 p90 pointwise). Result: max width deviation 12.2% relative (0.0120 abs) at S1c 46, under the raster floor — a documented residual attributed to the reference's raster provenance, not tuned away.python src/validate_bands.py --config ws2024 --band er --er-spectrum {decisions.calibration_er_spectrum} --reference {inputs.lz_ws2024_band_reference} --header {inputs.lz_nest_header_ws2024} --output {output}

Same WS2024 version bridges as er_band_validation_ws2024 (tuned header vectors, absolute-Fano [6] = 0.3, [8]/[9] swap, vector-driven skewness, ROI S2c >= 493 phd). ACCEPTANCE: band median within 5% relative (achieved: max 0.64%); band width within 5% relative OR 0.015 absolute in log10(S2c) (the raster reference's own curve resolution). Result: max width deviation 13.8% relative (0.0120 abs) over S1c 40-61 — a systematic, reference-side residual, root-caused and not tuned away: our engine gives nearly identical NR half-widths under the ws2022 and ws2024 parameter sets at fixed S1c (differences <= 0.005 abs), and the slide band is itself ~1.10-1.13x wider there than LZ's own published WS2022 paper band (which our engine reproduces at its usual 4-7%); the slide band's construction is unpublished — plausibly position-dependent broadening (S1/S2 correction residuals) absent under uniform_1d, the escalation path to simplified_position anticipated in the decision space.python src/validate_bands.py --config ws2024 --band nr --reference {inputs.lz_ws2024_band_reference} --header {inputs.lz_nest_header_ws2024} --output {output}
efficiency_passthrough Validation 3: staged efficiency curve passthroughfigureSanity check that the staged public efficiency inputs are ingested faithfully: overlay the pre-ROI orange Fig. 2 stage (S2 trigger + SS reconstruction/data-analysis cuts) and the HEPData black cumulative total (then adds S2 ROI and S1 ROI). Under input_pre_roi_curve only the orange curve is applied before NEST; the explicit observable ROI is applied once. ACCEPTANCE: values are taken directly from the declared input files; independently digitized Fig. 2 black versus HEPData t4 max absolute residual <=0.01 on common support; HEPData total E50 at 5.4 +/- 0.1 keVnr. The plot does not derive a pre-ROI curve by dividing cumulative efficiencies.python src/plot_efficiency.py --input {inputs.lz_efficiency_curve} --staged-input {inputs.lz_fig2_efficiency} --efficiency-treatment {decisions.efficiency_treatment} --output {output}
background_models Per-component background modelsdataEvery Table I background source (decision background_components.all_table1) propagated through the calibrated response into a 2D distribution in (S1c, log10 S2c) in the WS2024 ROI, normalized to its Table I pre-fit count for the combined single exposure (decision exposure_structure.combined_single). Response is the validated GetYields -> GetQuanta -> GetS1/GetS2 nestpy chain from the WS2024 HEPData header (lz_nest_header_ws2024; g2 gate 34.0 +/- 0.2 from CalculateG2), uniform_1d (decision detector_effects.uniform_1d) in corrected space. Energy spectra: 9 sources as digitized 2018-paper curves (lz2018_component_spectra, neutron shape from lz_neutron_spectrum_2018), tritium+14C as an 8:1 weighted mixture of analytic beta spectra, 124Xe as a 2-line EC model (10.00/5.98 keV by branch ratio) and 127Xe/125Xe as the 5.2 keV EC line (REVIEW ITEM — the composite Qy uses the published EC recombination enhancement Qy^L/Qy^beta = 0.87 +/- 0.03), both pushed through the response with the quanta-boundary EC charge suppression (S2 from q_ec x Ne via GetS2, recombination photons added to S1c as a Gaussian — exact in the mean, subdominant to the +/-0.03 published uncertainty on q). NR sources (atm nu, 8B+hep by pre-response efficiency-folded spectral-integral weighting, detector neutrons) use the selected efficiency_treatment input before response by rejection, followed by NEST and the explicit corrected-space ROI once. Under input_pre_roi_curve this is the orange Fig. 2 trigger + SS/data-analysis stage (lz_fig2_efficiency), not the total black curve (lz_efficiency_curve); the legacy alternative is for the declared matched A/B only. Both modes retain the 8B:hep mixture fraction, per-isotope stage counts, and generation/ROI acceptances. Display samples are proportionally renormalized to Table I after any thinning; full unthinned generation histograms and their MC variances are retained separately for shape control; detector_neutrons has Table I mean 0.0 and carries zero physical weight, so its shape comparisons are unit-area. ER sources sampled in true energy use the selected er_efficiency_treatment. The baseline staged chain is trigger B(E) before NEST, native threefold coincidence plus explicit S1c>3, then one conditional G(E)/Y(E) SS/analysis rejection at the retained true energy. G is total-1D t3 only where the user identified green/black overlap through 15 keV, then constant G(15)=0.959. The remaining corrected-space ROI (S1c<80, S2c>=493, log10 S2c<4.5) follows exactly once, with no additional coincidence/raw-S2/total-efficiency factor and no energy reconstruction/unfolding. The legacy ER mode applies only the explicit full ROI and is for this comparison. Each energy-space ER source has its own seeded stream; accepted event multiplicities and shapes change, but fixed Table-I physical means do not. This is an energy-conditional average acceptance, not a model of unpublished S1c/S2c/position-dependent reconstruction quality. The accidentals component is modeled in observable space from the factorized-contour reconstruction under decision accidentals_model.factorized_contour_constrained: P(S1c, log10 S2c) = f1(S1c) x f2(log10 S2c) with the marginals fitted to the WS2024 Fig. 3 68%/95% contours (level-set system with gauge and a c68-c95 = 1 gap anchor; sharpening exponent set by bisection so the enclosed volume is 68%; contour rms 0.293 dex, data-side — the figure's contours are not exactly factorized level sets; 95% enclosed volume 0.965 as the consistency check; fitted S1c marginal agrees with the SR1 Fig. 12 marginal to 0.09 dex median / 0.49 max over the matched support; tail beyond S1c = 60 extrapolated with floored log-slope). Edge-clipped contour points are dropped from the fit. Accidentals and detector-neutron sources are modeled from their published descriptions (data-driven in LZ).python src/build_background_models.py --output {output} --spectra {inputs.lz2018_component_spectra} --neutron-spectrum {inputs.lz_neutron_spectrum_2018} --efficiency {inputs.lz_efficiency_curve} --fig2-efficiency {inputs.lz_fig2_efficiency} --efficiency-treatment {decisions.efficiency_treatment} --er-staged-efficiency {inputs.lz_ws2024_er_staged_efficiency} --er-1d-efficiency {inputs.lz_ws2024_er_1d_efficiency} --er-efficiency-treatment {decisions.er_efficiency_treatment} --table1 {inputs.lz_table1_counts_reference} --contours {inputs.lz_ws2024_accidentals_contours} --sr1-marginals {inputs.lz_accidentals_marginals_sr1} --nest-header {inputs.lz_nest_header_ws2024} --background-components {decisions.background_components} --exposure-structure {decisions.exposure_structure} --nest-parameter-set {decisions.nest_parameter_set} --detector-effects {decisions.detector_effects} --accidentals-model {decisions.accidentals_model}
background_projection_validation Validation 4: background spectra vs LZfigureValidation of the background stage: our combined background model projected in LZ Fig. 4's band-projected coordinate u = (log10(S2c) - mu_ER(S1c)) / sigma_ER(S1c) (mu/sigma from the response_model_calibration ER band quantiles, themselves validated against LZ's published bands) and compared per category against the digitized Fig. 4 outlines (lz_ws2024_fig4_projection), over both S1c panels (3-40 and 40-80 phd). Category mapping: pb214 <- 214Pb; other ER as drawn <- kr85 + 136Xe (LZ's drawn outline holds only these two — solar-nu/212Pb/tritium appear only in their Total); xe124; xe127+125; accidentals; b8 <- 8B+hep+atm+neutrons; the full other-ER sum is also computed and expected to sit ~+0.1-0.3 dex above the drawn outline. ACCEPTANCE: (1) total ROI counts consistent with 1210 +/- 91; (2) per-component totals equal their Table I means; (3) panel-integrated totals within 20% of the digitized sums (a genuine prediction — the S1c split is not in Table I); (4) total-curve shape within rms 0.15 dex over bins with LZ level >= 1 event/bin (below that the drawn line's own thickness against the 10^-2 floor dominates and the bins carry <= 0.1% each); (5) per-category rms <= 0.25 dex over the same bins, with 124Xe evaluated at the best Qy_LL/Qy_beta within LZ's published floating prior [0.65, 0.87] (our pre-fit value is the TI box model 0.65; the drawn pre-fit figure implies ~0.7-0.8 — reported, and a natural knob for the later background-variation studies); (6) the total curve's absolute sub-floor tail within 8 events (~0.7% of the model; the deep low-charge tail is where LZ's full position-dependent simulation diverges from uniform_1d, the same attribution as the WS2024 NR mid-range width residual, covered by the simplified_position escalation universe). Sidecar JSON carries the full numeric comparison. The red curve shows 124Xe at the Fig.-4 shape-optimal q = 0.78 (presentation choice; LZ fit 0.70 +/- 0.04); the gates use the stored q = 0.65 model except gate 5's 124Xe entry. nr_efficiency_comparison Matched NR efficiency correction comparisondataBefore/after comparison of the pre-response NR efficiency treatment. Regenerates the complete matched-seed 12-source models in private temporary storage under both legacy total-curve and corrected pre-ROI selections, using the same response, actual sampling budgets and one explicit corrected-space ROI. Checks byte-for-byte that the active temporary model matches background_models, that all non-NR source arrays and metadata match across modes except for the intentional per-source efficiency_treatment mode label, and that full-count generation histograms reconcile with ROI multiplicities and Table I normalization. Archives retained event samples and weights, full histograms and MC variances, stage acceptances, efficiency curves, all Validation 4 JSON metrics, unit-area S1c/log10-S2c/u shapes, and an independent-seed fivefold-budget B8+hep comparison. Conditional unit-area shape differences use per-mode multinomial MC variances, without claiming exact cancellation after matched-seed rejection streams diverge. Physical Table I means are fixed; detector-neutron zero-weight shapes are compared unit-area. No acceptance gate requires Fig. 4 agreement to improve; the reconstructed corrected model must pass the same six exclusive-total Validation 4 gates.python src/compare_nr_efficiency.py --output {output} --background-models {inputs.background_models} --response {inputs.response_model_calibration} --validation-script {inputs.background_projection_script} --reference {inputs.lz_ws2024_fig4_projection} --spectra {inputs.lz2018_component_spectra} --neutron-spectrum {inputs.lz_neutron_spectrum_2018} --efficiency {inputs.lz_efficiency_curve} --fig2-efficiency {inputs.lz_fig2_efficiency} --efficiency-treatment {decisions.efficiency_treatment} --er-staged-efficiency {inputs.lz_ws2024_er_staged_efficiency} --er-1d-efficiency {inputs.lz_ws2024_er_1d_efficiency} --er-efficiency-treatment {decisions.er_efficiency_treatment} --table1 {inputs.lz_table1_counts_reference} --contours {inputs.lz_ws2024_accidentals_contours} --sr1-marginals {inputs.lz_accidentals_marginals_sr1} --nest-header {inputs.lz_nest_header_ws2024} --background-components {decisions.background_components} --exposure-structure {decisions.exposure_structure} --nest-parameter-set {decisions.nest_parameter_set} --detector-effects {decisions.detector_effects} --accidentals-model {decisions.accidentals_model}
nr_efficiency_validation Validation: NR pre-ROI efficiency correctionfigureVisualization and acceptance summary of nr_efficiency_comparison: pre-ROI and total efficiency curves with their exact staged meanings, pre-efficiency and conditional-ROI acceptances, and MC-aware corrected-minus-legacy unit-area NR shapes. Includes the independent-seed fivefold-statistics B8+hep comparison and Validation 4 gates for both modes. Legacy shapes are diagnostic only; the corrected chain is recoil-energy sampling -> Fig. 2 pre-ROI selection -> NEST -> one explicit ROI -> Table I normalization. Physical central counts do not change under this correction.python src/plot_nr_efficiency.py --input {inputs.nr_efficiency_comparison} --efficiency-treatment {decisions.efficiency_treatment} --output {output}
er_efficiency_comparison Complete staged ER efficiency comparisondataMatched-budget old/new comparison of all eight energy-space ER backgrounds within complete twelve-source models. The staged chain is sampled true energy -> public trigger B(E) -> NEST native threefold coincidence -> explicit S1c>3 -> one conditional C(E)=G(E)/Y(E) at the retained true energy -> remaining corrected-observable ROI exactly once -> Table I normalization. G uses the public t3 curve through the user-confirmed green/black overlap at 15 keV and the 0.959 plateau above it; Y constructs the conditional and is an independent forward diagnostic. The legacy mode has no energy-space ER selection before the explicit full ROI. Both modes archive all source samples, full/display MC multiplicities, full MC histograms and variances, stage acceptances, support/plateau counts, unit-area S1c/log10-S2c/u shapes, and both runs of the same six exclusive-total Validation-4 gates. No physical Table-I mean changes; simulation counts and effective sample sizes are distinct from physical rates. All three NR event samples and the observable-space accidentals must be identical across modes, apart from the intentional ER-mode metadata label. Accidentals never pass through an energy-space ER chain. The fixed-energy cumulative-Y and independent total-2D t4 checks use 5000 NEST samples per 0.25-keV energy point; central-curve tolerance is 0.02 plus two finite-MC binomial sigmas, explicitly not a recovered HEPData covariance. t4 is never multiplied into production, no agreement improvement is required, and residual disagreement is retained as evidence about central-curve extraction and the energy-conditional approximation.python src/compare_er_efficiency.py --output {output} --background-models {inputs.background_models} --response {inputs.response_model_calibration} --validation-script {inputs.background_projection_script} --reference {inputs.lz_ws2024_fig4_projection} --er-2d-efficiency {inputs.lz_ws2024_er_2d_efficiency} --forward-check-statistics 5000 --spectra {inputs.lz2018_component_spectra} --neutron-spectrum {inputs.lz_neutron_spectrum_2018} --efficiency {inputs.lz_efficiency_curve} --fig2-efficiency {inputs.lz_fig2_efficiency} --efficiency-treatment {decisions.efficiency_treatment} --er-staged-efficiency {inputs.lz_ws2024_er_staged_efficiency} --er-1d-efficiency {inputs.lz_ws2024_er_1d_efficiency} --er-efficiency-treatment {decisions.er_efficiency_treatment} --table1 {inputs.lz_table1_counts_reference} --contours {inputs.lz_ws2024_accidentals_contours} --sr1-marginals {inputs.lz_accidentals_marginals_sr1} --nest-header {inputs.lz_nest_header_ws2024} --background-components {decisions.background_components} --exposure-structure {decisions.exposure_structure} --nest-parameter-set {decisions.nest_parameter_set} --detector-effects {decisions.detector_effects} --accidentals-model {decisions.accidentals_model}
er_efficiency_validation Validation: staged ER efficiency, shapes, and independent diagnosticsfigureVisualization of er_efficiency_comparison: public trigger/cumulative-S1/G curves, exact conditional G/Y construction, independent fixed-energy cumulative-Y and total-2D comparisons, stage-count table distinguishing MC multiplicities from fixed Table-I physical counts, both Fig.-4 exclusive totals with their model-only finite-MC shaded bands, and full-histogram unit-shape differences for every one of the eight ER sources in S1c, log10 S2c and u. New/old identity uses color plus line style; both light and dark renders are inspected. No dual axes, no t4 product, no claim of physical-rate change or required improvement against LZ.python src/plot_er_efficiency.py --input {inputs.er_efficiency_comparison} --response {inputs.response_model_calibration} --reference {inputs.lz_ws2024_fig4_projection} --er-efficiency-treatment {decisions.er_efficiency_treatment} --output {output}
wimp_signal_models Absolute WS2024 WIMP signal templatesdataExactly the 26 published SI-reference mass rows propagated through the validated WS2024 chain: native NEST WIMP recoil sampling -> only the public Fig. 2 pre-ROI trigger+SS/data-analysis efficiency -> unchanged NEST NR response -> exactly one corrected-space ROI (3<S1c<80 phd, S2c>=493 phd, log10 S2c<4.5) -> absolute native yield at the native SI per-nucleon 1e-36 cm2 reference and 3.3 WS2024 tonne-years. No Table-I normalization, LZ-background/cross-section fit, published total ROI efficiency, raw-S2 re-cut, or WS2024 exposure scaling. This is the WS2024 component, not a 4.2/3.3-scaled combined exposure: a future 4.2-tonne-year model must add a separately validated 0.9-tonne-year WS2022 response, efficiency, ROI and component-specific backgrounds. Native SHM conventions are fixed (rho0=0.3 GeV/cm3, v0=238 km/s, vesc=544 km/s, V_SUN=250.2 km/s), not profiled. The representative-day scalar Earth-speed approximation and its directly generated 12-phase 40 GeV/c2 control are retained, not a phase-resolved analysis. Native >100 keVnr tail use and 500-5000 keVnr unadded guards are explicit per wimp_native_support; native WIMP_dRate tail integration is separate from NEST detector-response evaluation, which emits its beyond-AmBe-endpoint warnings above 300 keV at high masses (stored as a limitation rather than hidden). Every mass retains full integer MC and physical-weight (S1c,log10S2c) histograms and variances, both full Fig.-4 projections, generation/selection/ROI energy records, source/patch provenance, native integration/grid/isotope metadata, and tail stages. Display samples are separately capped and preserved; they never determine absolute yield. A future PLR/FC stage consumes this archive; neither is implemented here.python src/build_wimp_signal_models.py --header {inputs.lz_nest_header_ws2024} --efficiency {inputs.lz_fig2_efficiency} --response {inputs.response_model_calibration} --sensitivity {inputs.lz_si_sensitivity_reference} --fig4-reference {inputs.lz_ws2024_fig4_projection} --output {output} --annual-comparison --response-model {decisions.response_model} --time-mode {decisions.wimp_time_treatment} --support-treatment {decisions.wimp_native_support} --efficiency-treatment {decisions.efficiency_treatment} --exposure-structure {decisions.exposure_structure} --nest-parameter-set {decisions.nest_parameter_set} --detector-effects {decisions.detector_effects} --halo-model {decisions.halo_model}
wimp_fig4_validation WIMP checkpoint: absolute 40 GeV/c2 yield vs LZ Fig. 4figureTwo-panel Fig.-4-style comparison at 40 GeV/c2 in the validated WS2024 configuration at 3.3 tonne-years. The native absolute model is multiplied ONLY by 2.1816833824484827e-48 / 1e-36, reading the exact tabulated observed power-constrained SI limit from lz_si_sensitivity_reference; median 5.0587223537493065e-48 is explicitly rejected for this display. This is the requested display convention, not a refit, a power-constraint calculation, a claim to rediscover LZ's drawn amplitude, or permission to tune the model. Show the sparse purple LZ reference, absolute this-work line and model-only finite-MC uncertainty band, with model-minus-LZ residual panels. The existing reference has 8 top and 3 bottom above-floor rows; clipped entries remain missing, never zero. Report comparable-bin model/LZ sums and signed residuals, peak displacement, all-grid and reference-absent model weight separately in wimp_fig4_validation_metrics; no background one-event/bin dex-RMS gate or LZ background-band uncertainty is applied to the WIMP. This is a descriptive go/no-go checkpoint: any unresolved normalization/shape problem must be reported, not tuned or hidden.python src/validate_wimp_signal.py --models {inputs.wimp_signal_models} --response {inputs.response_model_calibration} --fig4-reference {inputs.lz_ws2024_fig4_projection} --sensitivity {inputs.lz_si_sensitivity_reference} --output {output} --require-full-grid --response-model {decisions.response_model} --time-mode {decisions.wimp_time_treatment} --support-treatment {decisions.wimp_native_support} --efficiency-treatment {decisions.efficiency_treatment} --exposure-structure {decisions.exposure_structure} --nest-parameter-set {decisions.nest_parameter_set} --detector-effects {decisions.detector_effects} --halo-model {decisions.halo_model}
wimp_fig4_validation_metrics Numerical 40 GeV/c2 Fig.-4 validationdataSeparately declared one-file JSON companion to wimp_fig4_validation (not a silent PNG sidecar). Records the exact native reference/display limits, native rate, absolute full-ROI and displayed yields, MC precision and direct/acceptance yield closures, complete per-bin model/LZ/residual arrays, comparable-bin signed sums, reference-absent model weights, peak displacement, full integer-grid/ER-band dependency checks, active-decision checks and the 40 GeV/c2 representative-vs-annual response diagnostic. Reference-limited diagnostics and missing-reference handling are explicit; no artificial acceptance improvement target is introduced.python src/validate_wimp_signal.py --models {inputs.wimp_signal_models} --response {inputs.response_model_calibration} --fig4-reference {inputs.lz_ws2024_fig4_projection} --sensitivity {inputs.lz_si_sensitivity_reference} --output {output} --require-full-grid --response-model {decisions.response_model} --time-mode {decisions.wimp_time_treatment} --support-treatment {decisions.wimp_native_support} --efficiency-treatment {decisions.efficiency_treatment} --exposure-structure {decisions.exposure_structure} --nest-parameter-set {decisions.nest_parameter_set} --detector-effects {decisions.detector_effects} --halo-model {decisions.halo_model}
wimp_fig3_validation WIMP checkpoint: 40 GeV/c2 signal region vs LZ Fig. 3figureValidation beyond the original six: the 40 GeV/c2 WIMP's 2D morphology in (S1c, log10 S2c) against the purple 68%/95% regions of WS2024 Fig. 3 (All Data, arXiv:2410.17036v3), extracted exactly from the pinned paper's vector paths. Left: our full 59,852-event ROI MC histogram (archive grid, 1 phd x 0.02 dex) under LZ's regions. Right: our own 68%/95% highest-density contours of a display-only smoothed copy (1.1 phd, 0.040 dex) against LZ's, with the containment of our ROI sample inside LZ's regions (unbinned, on the uniform 50,000-event display subsample; measured 65.9% +/- 0.2% in the 68% region and 94.4% +/- 0.1% in the 95% region). Complements wimp_fig4_validation (1D band projection, absolute yield) with the 2D shape. ACCEPTANCE (user decision 2026-11-19): containment inside LZ's 68% region within 0.68 +/- 0.05 and inside the 95% region within 0.95 +/- 0.03 (absolute fractions). This is a tolerance, not a significance test: published regions are not a 2D PDF and LZ's contour uncertainty is unavailable; the pull against our MC sigma alone (about -10 and -6) is reported but not gated. The verdict is printed on the figure. No refit, renormalization or new production; ROI 3 < S1c < 80 phd, S2c >= 493 phd, log10 S2c < 4.5.python src/plot_wimp_fig3_comparison.py --models {inputs.wimp_signal_models} --paper {inputs.lz_ws2024_paper} --output {output}
wimp_fig3_validation_metrics Numerical 40 GeV/c2 Fig.-3 region comparisondataOne-file JSON companion to wimp_fig3_validation: the acceptance verdict (per region: nominal, tolerance, measured, deviation, pull vs MC sigma, pass), LZ polygon vertices and bounds, containment fractions with binomial MC sigma, fractions at S1c > 40 and log10 S2c < 2.75, central quantiles, our contour levels and smoothing, the 2026-11-13 event-level scratch values (66.00% / 94.37%) for reference, and cautions.python src/plot_wimp_fig3_comparison.py --models {inputs.wimp_signal_models} --paper {inputs.lz_ws2024_paper} --output {output}
plr_sensitivity_curve 2D PLR median sensitivity curvetablePrimary sensitivity result: the binned 2D profile likelihood in (S1c, log10 S2c) with background-rate nuisance parameters, raster-scanned over WIMP mass. Columns: WIMP mass, median expected limit from background-only toys (decision median_sensitivity_definition.median_of_toy_limits), +/-1 and +/-2 sigma band edges, with the power constraint applied (decision power_constraint.applied_1sigma) and two-sided test statistic (decision test_statistic_sidedness.two_sided). Toy settings: 25 geometric mu points 0.5-40 signal events, 2000 signal toys per mu, 1000 background-only toys, seed 20261118. Also stores the bootstrap sigma of the median and the UNCONSTRAINED median and band edges (LZ's band convention; the PC -2 sigma edge repeats -1 sigma). Exposure is the WS2024 3.3 t-y of the signal archive and Table I. ACCEPTANCE: compared against the LZ WS2024-only reference in sensitivity_vs_lz_validation.python src/plr_scan.py --signal {inputs.wimp_signal_models} --background {inputs.background_models} --mu-min 0.5 --mu-max 40 --mu-points 25 --toys-per-mu 2000 --bkg-toys 1000 --workers 8 --seed 20261118 --output-csv {output} --statistics {decisions.statistics} --background-components {decisions.background_components} --exposure-structure {decisions.exposure_structure} --median-sensitivity-definition {decisions.median_sensitivity_definition} --power-constraint {decisions.power_constraint} --test-statistic-sidedness {decisions.test_statistic_sidedness}
fc_sensitivity_curve Cut-and-count FC sensitivity curvetableCross-check result: cut-and-count in the (S1c, log10 S2c) ROI using direct FC_ints(n,b,alpha=0.1) calls from colleague_feldman_cousins_script. For each selected region, the fixed expected background is the sum of full physical background hist_counts and an observed toy is N~Poisson(mu_signal+B), with background-only toys N~Poisson(B). The FC interval is in signal-event units on the source's native 0.005-event grid; do not confuse it with scipy.stats.poisson.ppf, a count quantile. Median sensitivity is the median of background-only signal-event limits (decision median_sensitivity_definition.median_of_toy_limits). For counting this is computed exactly without toys: the FC upper limit is non-decreasing in n at fixed B (assert it), so the median limit equals FC_ints at the Poisson(B) median count (smallest n with CDF >= 0.5), and band edges are FC_ints at the corresponding Poisson count quantiles. Toys would only add Monte Carlo noise; the 2D PLR, whose test statistic is not a function of one count, still needs toys. Convert using sigma_UL=1e-36*mu_UL/mu_WIMP(region;1e-36 cm2), where mu_WIMP is the sum of the absolute signal hist_counts selected in that region at 3.3 WS2024 tonne-years. The absolute production efficiency, exposure and ROI are already included exactly once in that yield; do not apply another efficiency/exposure factor or Table-I-style normalization. Apply the one-sigma power constraint at result assembly (decision power_constraint.applied_1sigma). Region per mass: progressive voxel ranking by s_i/b_i (fc_region_scan_script), the region minimizing the median PC limit is chosen. Columns: mass, PC median and +-1/2 sigma edges, unconstrained median, region background, retained signal fraction, n_med, region bin count. Exposure is WS2024 3.3 t-y.python src/fc_region_scan.py --signal {inputs.wimp_signal_models} --background {inputs.background_models} --response {inputs.response_model_calibration} --fc-source {inputs.colleague_feldman_cousins_script} --output-csv {output} --statistics {decisions.statistics} --background-components {decisions.background_components} --exposure-structure {decisions.exposure_structure} --median-sensitivity-definition {decisions.median_sensitivity_definition} --power-constraint {decisions.power_constraint} --test-statistic-sidedness {decisions.test_statistic_sidedness}
sensitivity_vs_lz_validation Validation 5: median sensitivity vs LZ WS2024-onlyfigureThe headline validation, like-for-like: our PLR median sensitivity curve (unconstrained +/-1 and +/-2 sigma toy bands, PC median) overlaid on LZ's WS2024-only (3.3 t-y) curves from slide 24 (lz_ws2024_only_sensitivity_reference), the right target for our WS2024 exposure; the combined 4.2 t-y 5.1e-48 (lz_si_sensitivity_reference) is NOT the target (user decision 2026-11-18). The FC counting median is overlaid for reference. ACCEPTANCE: A1 - at 40 GeV/c2 our PC median is within 25% of LZ's WS2024-only median (5.76e-48), |ours/LZ - 1| <= 0.25 (user decision 2026-11-19, replacing the original |ours - LZ| <= 2 x bootstrap-sigma gate, which ignored the uncertainty of LZ's curve and its digitization and the binned single-sample likelihood approximation; it failed at ratio 0.935, pull -3.5, and the pull is still reported informationally); A2 - at every mass where LZ's +/-1 sigma band is published (finite; 13-10000 GeV/c2), our PC median lies inside it. Both verdicts are printed and written on the figure.python src/plot_plr_scan.py --scan {inputs.plr_sensitivity_curve} --fc {inputs.fc_sensitivity_curve} --reference {inputs.lz_ws2024_only_sensitivity_reference} --output {output} --statistics {decisions.statistics} --median-sensitivity-definition {decisions.median_sensitivity_definition} --power-constraint {decisions.power_constraint} --test-statistic-sidedness {decisions.test_statistic_sidedness}
fc_plr_crosscheck Validation 6: FC cross-check vs PLRfigureInternal statistical validation: the FC cut-and-count sensitivity curve overlaid on the 2D PLR curve. ACCEPTANCE: the two curves agree within their combined band widths over the mass range where the ROI cut-and-count retains efficiency; systematic disagreement localizes to the likelihood approximation, not the microphysics. Operationalized: at every mass |ln(PLR/FC)| <= sqrt(w_PLR^2 + w_FC^2), w = ln(plus1sigma/median) of each method (upper edges, because the power constraint and the n_med = 0 counting regime pin the lower edges to the median); the FC retained signal fraction is reported.python src/plot_fc_plr_crosscheck.py --plr {inputs.plr_sensitivity_curve} --fc {inputs.fc_sensitivity_curve} --output {output} --statistics {decisions.statistics} --median-sensitivity-definition {decisions.median_sensitivity_definition} --power-constraint {decisions.power_constraint} --test-statistic-sidedness {decisions.test_statistic_sidedness}
plr_sensitivity_curve_1000d Extension: 2D PLR median sensitivity at 1000 live daystableExposure extension (no LZ reference): the plr_sensitivity_curve construction with signal and every Table-I mean scaled by k = 1000/220 = 4.545454545454546 (WS2024's 220 live days -> 1000), and each Table-I constraint width scaled by the same k (fixed fractional uncertainty, the conservative choice). Same signal/background templates, so the same response, efficiency and ROI. 28 geometric mu points 0.5-60 signal events (the band moves up in signal events with exposure), 2000 toys per mu, 1000 background-only toys, seed 20261118. Columns as in plr_sensitivity_curve, exposure_scale = k.python src/plr_scan.py --signal {inputs.wimp_signal_models} --background {inputs.background_models} --exposure-scale 4.545454545454546 --mu-min 0.5 --mu-max 60 --mu-points 28 --toys-per-mu 2000 --bkg-toys 1000 --workers 8 --seed 20261118 --output-csv {output} --statistics {decisions.statistics} --background-components {decisions.background_components} --exposure-structure {decisions.exposure_structure} --median-sensitivity-definition {decisions.median_sensitivity_definition} --power-constraint {decisions.power_constraint} --test-statistic-sidedness {decisions.test_statistic_sidedness}
fc_sensitivity_curve_1000d Extension: FC counting median sensitivity at 1000 live daystableExposure extension (no LZ reference): the fc_sensitivity_curve construction with signal and background expectations scaled by k = 1000/220 = 4.545454545454546; the counting region is re-optimized per mass at the scaled expectations. Columns as in fc_sensitivity_curve.python src/fc_region_scan.py --signal {inputs.wimp_signal_models} --background {inputs.background_models} --response {inputs.response_model_calibration} --fc-source {inputs.colleague_feldman_cousins_script} --exposure-scale 4.545454545454546 --output-csv {output} --statistics {decisions.statistics} --background-components {decisions.background_components} --exposure-structure {decisions.exposure_structure} --median-sensitivity-definition {decisions.median_sensitivity_definition} --power-constraint {decisions.power_constraint} --test-statistic-sidedness {decisions.test_statistic_sidedness}
plr_fc_exposure_comparison Extension: does the likelihood beat cut-and-count as exposure grows?figurePLR and FC counting medians at 220 and 1000 live days with the PLR unconstrained +-1 sigma band, and the PLR/FC median ratio per exposure. Descriptive, no acceptance gate and no LZ reference. Expectation recorded from the scratch study (2026-11-18): PLR/FC ~0.95-1.05 at 220 d; 0.81-0.93 above ~19 GeV/c2 at 1000 d, where the FC optimum still sits at n_med = 0 and gives up signal fraction while the PLR uses the whole plane.python src/plot_plr_exposure.py --run '220 live days,{inputs.plr_sensitivity_curve},{inputs.fc_sensitivity_curve}' --run '1000 live days,{inputs.plr_sensitivity_curve_1000d},{inputs.fc_sensitivity_curve_1000d}' --output {output} --statistics {decisions.statistics} --median-sensitivity-definition {decisions.median_sensitivity_definition} --power-constraint {decisions.power_constraint} --test-statistic-sidedness {decisions.test_statistic_sidedness}
